fields.Participants: HQ Function Mgr, VP Store Operations, Store Manager
fields.Trigger: HQ function creates task for stores

Automation Opportunity: - Task auto-created from the template (W2370); assignment auto-targeted; status auto-tracked
Controls: - Operational: VP Store Operations task-volume oversight; HQ Function Manager priority-discipline
Pain Points / Risks: - **Task-overload risk**: HQ functions each create tasks without awareness of the cumulative volume, overwhelming stores; mitigated by the W2378 information-overload assessment and the task-volume coordination (VP Store Operations visible on total task load)

- **Vague-task risk**: a task with a vague description ("clean up the aisle") produces inconsistent execution; mitigated by the W2370 standardized task templates with clear steps and evidence requirements
System Touchpoints: - Task-management platform (links to VS-07 / W571 store-comms) — the task creation, assignment, and status tracking
- Store Manager app (links to VS-75) — the task-receiving and assignment channel
- Routing/targeting (links to VS-29 / W299 store-cluster) — the all/regional/specific targeting
Time Estimate: ~20 min/task × ~150/week + Store Manager acknowledgment absorbed = **~200 hours/month** HQ Function Managers distributed.

steps.activity: HQ Manager creates task: description, assigned stores (all/regional/specific), priority, category, deadline, required evidence (photo/checkbox/form), responsible role at store
System pushes to assigned stores; Store Manager acknowledges and assigns to responsible staff; system tracks status (assigned/in-progress/completed/overdue)

fields.Participants: Regional Ops Manager, Store Staff, HQ Function Mgr

Automation Opportunity: - Evidence auto-timestamped/geo-tagged; status auto-updated on submission
Controls: - CTL-419 (ensure controlled execution — Store Task Assignment & Compliance Tracking (PA-63.2).)
- Operational: Store Manager approval-before-submission (step 2); Regional Ops Mgr oversight
Pain Points / Risks: - **Deadline-miss risk**: a task slips past the deadline because of store-ops priority conflicts; mitigated by the internal-deadline-ahead-of-HQ in step 1 and the W2369 Regional follow-up
- **Evidence-fraud risk**: a store submits stale/fabricated evidence; mitigated by the timestamp/geo-tag on photos and the W2371 quality audit
System Touchpoints: - Task-management platform (links to VS-07 / W571, VS-75 app) — the task execution and evidence submission
- Store Manager app (links to VS-75) — the submission and approval channel
- Evidence capture (photo/form) — the completion documentation
Time Estimate: ~12 min/triage + execution varies × ~3 tasks/store/week × 200 stores = **~1,500–2,000 hours/month** Store teams (absorbed into store-ops).

steps.activity: Store Manager reviews task requirements; assigns to appropriate Department Supervisor or staff member; sets internal deadline ahead of HQ deadline
Staff executes task; documents completion with required evidence (photo, form, confirmation); submits via store manager app; Store Manager reviews and approves before submission to HQ

Automation Opportunity: - Dashboard auto-refreshed; overdue/non-responsive auto-flagged for Regional Ops
Controls: - Operational: VP Store Operations daily/weekly review; COO escalation on chronic non-compliance
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dashboard-noise risk**: the dashboard shows every task equally, drowning the critical ones; mitigated by the priority-segmented view and the overdue-foregrounding
- **Compliance-without-quality risk**: a store completes tasks (high compliance rate) but the quality is poor (rushed execution); mitigated by the W2371 quality audit alongside the rate metric
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113, VS-07 / W571 task platform) — the compliance dashboard
- Store-performance scorecard (links to VS-07 / W67) — the compliance score as a Store Manager KPI
- Alerting (links to VS-27 / W380) — the overdue/non-responsive auto-flag
Time Estimate: ~30 min/day + ~2.5 hours/week ≈ ~125 + ~130 hours = **~255 hours/year** VP Store Operations.

steps.activity: Dashboard: task completion rate by store, region, and function; overdue tasks highlighted; compliance score trending; non-responsive stores flagged for Regional Ops follow-up

fields.Participants: Regional Ops Manager, VP Store Operations
fields.Trigger: Store has overdue or non-compliant tasks

Automation Opportunity: - Overdue-task worklist auto-routed to Regional Ops; root-cause-category auto-tracked for pattern analysis
Controls: - CTL-419 (ensure controlled execution — Store Task Assignment & Compliance Tracking (PA-63.2).)
- Operational: VP Store Operations chronic-case escalation review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Follow-up-fatigue risk**: the same stores are chronically overdue, and Regional Ops follow-up becomes routine without resolving the root cause; mitigated by the root-cause determination in step 1 and the escalation for chronic cases
- **Punitive-only-follow-up risk**: follow-up is perceived as punitive, eroding Store Manager trust; mitigated by the support-orientation (root cause + support, not just enforcement)
System Touchpoints: - Task platform / overdue (links to VS-07 / W571, W2368 dashboard) — the overdue-task worklist
- Field-audit/follow-up tooling (links to VS-177 field-retail) — the Regional Ops follow-up channel
- Store-performance (links to VS-07 / W67) — the chronic-non-compliance pattern
Time Estimate: ~20 min/store × ~25/week ≈ ~500 min/week ≈ **~36 hours/month** Regional Ops Managers distributed.

steps.activity: Regional Ops Manager contacts Store Manager for overdue tasks; determines root cause (staffing, training, system issue); provides support or escalates to HQ

fields.Trigger: New task type creation or template update

Automation Opportunity: - Template library centrally governed; format-variants auto-derived from the master
Controls: - CTL-419 (ensure controlled execution — Store Task Assignment & Compliance Tracking (PA-63.2).)
- Operational: VP Store Operations template-library sign-off; COO review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Template-rigidity risk**: a template is so rigid it doesn't fit store-format variation (a compact store's task differs from a flagship's); mitigated by the format-variant templates where needed
- **Template-proliferation risk**: every HQ function creates its own templates, fragmenting the library; mitigated by the VP Store Operations standardization ownership (single library)
System Touchpoints: - Task template master (links to VS-29 / W301 promo-rule, W296 service-item master pattern) — the standardized templates
- Task platform (links to VS-07 / W571) — the template configuration
- IT config / change (links to VS-27 / W132) — the template releases
Time Estimate: ~1.5 days/quarter = **~50–60 hours/year** VP Store Operations + IT.

steps.activity: VP Store Operations standardizes task templates: predefined steps, required evidence, typical duration, responsible role; ensures consistency across HQ functions; IT configures in platform

fields.Participants: Regional Ops Manager, VP Store Operations

Automation Opportunity: - Sample auto-selected (risk-based); quality-score auto-fed to the scorecard
Controls: - CTL-419 (ensure controlled execution — Store Task Assignment & Compliance Tracking (PA-63.2).)
- operational: auditor independence — Regional Ops not the task creator; operational: VP Store Operations quality-trend review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Compliance-vs-quality-divergence risk**: a store has high completion rate but low quality (rushed/check-box execution); mitigated by the quality audit catching the divergence

- **Sample-size-limitation risk**: auditing 50 of ~600 monthly tasks is a small sample; mitigated by the risk-based sample (high-volume stores, high-stakes task types) and the chronic-quality-issue escalation
System Touchpoints: - Task platform / evidence (links to VS-07 / W571, W2367) — the submitted evidence
- Field-audit (links to VS-177 field-retail audit, VS-55 / W2174 planogram-compliance pattern) — the in-person verification
- Quality scorecard (links to VS-07 / W67) — the quality-audit score as a Store Manager KPI
Time Estimate: ~4 hours/month Regional Ops = **~50 hours/year** per Regional Ops Manager.

steps.activity: Regional Ops Manager audits a sample of completed tasks (photo evidence vs. actual store condition on a follow-up visit, or documentation review); scores quality on a rubric; provides feedback

Automation Opportunity: - Calendar auto-assembled from the seasonal planogram/promo/training dependencies; collision auto-detected
Controls: - CTL-419 (ensure controlled execution — Store Task Assignment & Compliance Tracking (PA-63.2).)
- Operational: Merchandising Planner calendar sign-off; VP Store Operations load-check
Pain Points / Risks: - **Task-collision risk**: seasonal tasks collide with regular tasks, overwhelming stores during the pre-season crunch; mitigated by the calendar-coordination (seasonal tasks windowed, regular tasks deferred)
- **Sequencing-error risk**: tasks are sequenced out of order (display setup before planogram reset), producing rework; mitigated by the dependency-aware sequencing in the calendar
System Touchpoints: - Task calendar (links to VS-07 / W571, VS-29 / W306 seasonal-calendar master) — the seasonal task sequencing
- Seasonal package (links to VS-64 / W2382, VS-63 / W2364) — the bundled distribution
- Store-comms (links to VS-07 / W571) — the calendar communication

steps.activity: Merchandising Coordinator plans the seasonal task calendar: planogram reset, display setup, pricing update, training, promo launch sequenced against the season-start date; distributes 3 weeks ahead via W2364

Automation Opportunity: - Analytics auto-refreshed; chronic-bottleneck auto-flagged for the quarterly review
Controls: - CTL-419 (ensure controlled execution — Store Task Assignment & Compliance Tracking (PA-63.2).)
- Operational: Analytics Manager methodology sign-off; VP Store Operations quarterly-improvement-review sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-without-action risk**: the analytics surface bottlenecks but no one fixes them; mitigated by the quarterly improvement review requiring a fix-decision per finding

- **Blame-the-store risk**: the analysis attributes low completion to store failure when the root cause is task-design (vague template, unrealistic deadline); mitigated by the task-design lens in the analysis
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113, VS-07 / W571 task platform) — the task-performance dataset
- Process improvement (links to VS-133 / OpEx process mining) — the systemic-bottleneck analysis
- Task templates (links to VS-63 / W2370) — the fix applied to the template when the analysis identifies a task-design issue

steps.activity: Analytics Manager analyzes the task data: completion rate, on-time rate, quality score by function/category/store; identifies systemic bottlenecks (a task type with chronically low completion) and recommends process fixes
